findings_not_failures.finding: 66c62129 exempts 7 lattice pixels of the threshold-128 case from GPU-vs-pigment parity (they may be 0 or 1; a NOT_PROVEN line counts them) on the SD-12 premise that the CPU reference evaluates in binary64 and the GPU in binary32. That premise is false: pigment's Threshold is binary32 end to end (adjust_math.rs:807 apply(rgb: [f32; 3]), :878 lum(rgb) >= level - THRESHOLD_HALF_CODE, blend_math.rs:463 lum(c: [f32; 3]) -> f32), and kernel.wgsl:361-363 evaluates the same binary32 formula (hsk_lum :50-52). The ties exist since 3d5fbdae (SMB-D5-PS-COMPARE) moved the cut from level to level - 0.5/255 = 0.5 on the PS-C07 oracle reading round(255 lum) >= level; the test comment written at c5bd9be1 for the old cut ('no lattice luminance ties it') hid them: 30i + 59j + 11k = 800 has exactly 7 solutions on the 17^3 i/16 lattice (validator count). At a tie pigment gives white (the lane's run1 at (129, 0): want 1.0, got 0.0), as real arithmetic and round-half-up of the oracle reading do; DX12 agreed with pigment (probe log max_err 0), the Vulkan kernel returns 0. So the tie answer follows an oracle-backed reading rather than being undefined, and on the product backend (Vulkan) the GPU deviates there. The set is not measure-zero for quantized content: 1110 of 2^24 8-bit colours tie exactly at level 128 in real arithmetic (validator count; whether their binary32 evaluation also splits on Vulkan is UNVERIFIED). The NOT_PROVEN line counts boundary pixels, not how many of them differ from pigment.
findings_not_failures.repair_direction: make the WGSL threshold decide exact ties as pigment does (contraction-free or error-free luminance sum, or the integer round(255 lum) >= level of the PS-C07 reading) and restore exact parity at the 7 ties; until then print how many boundary pixels differ; correct SD-12's binary64 premise; the tie rule stays an Operator D5 decision

findings_not_failures.finding: MAX_EXPORT_INPUT_BYTES (2 GiB) bounds the encoded bytes of all --media and --audio files, but each --audio file is then decoded up to ImportLimits::max_frames (48000 x 3600 x 3 = 518.4M frames, about 4 GiB of planar f32 per stereo file) and the decoded total across files is not bounded; the number of --audio files is unbounded, and a compressible stream (FLAC constant subframes) can reach max_frames from a small file.
